snapshots.name: Ulysses
snapshots.body: King of Ithaca, renowned among the Greeks for his cunning, endurance, and gift for speech. Ten years after the fall of Troy he has still not returned home, and his household despairs of ever seeing him again.

snapshots.name: Penelope
snapshots.body: Odysseus's wife, who has held out for years against a hall full of suitors pressing her to remarry. She keeps her household together in Ithaca while awaiting news of her husband.

snapshots.name: Telemachus
snapshots.body: Son of Odysseus and Penelope, grown to young manhood during his father's long absence. He sets out from Ithaca in search of news of his father, unsettled by the suitors overrunning his home.

snapshots.name: Minerva
snapshots.body: Goddess of wisdom and war, Odysseus's steadfast divine patron throughout his years of wandering. She intervenes repeatedly on his and Telemachus's behalf, often in disguise.

snapshots.name: Neptune
snapshots.body: God of the sea, whose lasting anger at Odysseus is the chief obstacle to his voyage home. His hostility follows Odysseus across the seas even when the other gods would let him pass.

snapshots.name: Jove
snapshots.body: King of the gods, who presides over the divine council that debates Odysseus's fate. His word ultimately outweighs the objections of the gods opposed to Odysseus's return.

snapshots.name: Mercury
snapshots.body: Messenger of the gods, sent on errands that require swift and unseen passage between Olympus and the mortal world. He carries word of the gods' decisions to those who must obey them.

snapshots.name: Calypso
snapshots.body: A nymph who rules the remote island of Ogygia, where Odysseus has been detained for years. She wishes to keep him with her as her husband, against his own longing for home.

snapshots.name: Circe
snapshots.body: An enchantress who rules the island of Aeaea, skilled in transforming men who land there into beasts. Odysseus and his crew encounter her partway through their long voyage.

snapshots.name: Polyphemus
snapshots.body: A one-eyed Cyclops, son of the god of the sea, who traps Odysseus and his men in his cave on an island of giant shepherds. His blinding at Odysseus's hands is the origin of the sea-god's lasting grudge.

snapshots.name: the Sun-god
snapshots.body: The sun-god, who pastures sacred cattle on the island of Thrinacia. Odysseus is warned before he ever reaches the island to leave those herds untouched.

snapshots.name: Euryclea
snapshots.body: The elderly nurse who cared for Odysseus as a child and now serves in his household. Her long loyalty to the family makes her one of the few in the house Telemachus and Penelope fully trust.

snapshots.name: Eumaeus
snapshots.body: The swineherd who manages Odysseus's pigs in his master's long absence. His unwavering loyalty to the absent king survives years without news of whether Odysseus is alive at all.

snapshots.name: Antinous
snapshots.body: The most overbearing of the suitors camped in Odysseus's hall, pressing Penelope to choose a husband from among them. He treats the household's absent master with open contempt.

snapshots.name: Eurymachus
snapshots.body: A smooth-tongued suitor among those courting Penelope, second only to Antinous in his standing among them. He is quicker than most to mask his intentions with flattering words.

snapshots.name: Laertes
snapshots.body: Odysseus's aged father, who has withdrawn to a country farm and taken his son's long absence hard. He lives apart from the troubles overtaking the household in town.

snapshots.name: Nestor
snapshots.body: The elderly king of Pylos, a veteran of the war at Troy known for his long memory and readiness with counsel. Telemachus visits him in search of news of his father.

snapshots.name: Menelaus
snapshots.body: King of Sparta and Agamemnon's brother, whose own homecoming from Troy was long and difficult. He and his household host Telemachus during the young man's search for news of his father.

snapshots.name: Helen
snapshots.body: Queen of Sparta and wife of Menelaus, whose abduction to Troy years earlier had set off the war. She is at Menelaus's side, restored to her household, when Telemachus arrives.

snapshots.name: Nausicaa
snapshots.body: A Phaeacian princess, daughter of King Alcinous, who discovers the shipwrecked Odysseus washed up on her island's shore. Her kindness to the stranger opens the way to his welcome at her father's court.

snapshots.name: Alcinous
snapshots.body: King of the seafaring Phaeacians and father of Nausicaa. He receives the shipwrecked Odysseus as a guest and hears the story of his wanderings at his own table.

snapshots.name: Teiresias
snapshots.body: A blind prophet of Thebes, consulted by Odysseus among the shades of the dead. His guidance concerns the dangers and the way home that still lie ahead of Odysseus's voyage.

snapshots.name: Agamemnon
snapshots.body: The Greek commander-in-chief at Troy, encountered by Odysseus among the shades of the dead. His account of the homecoming that awaited him is a bitter warning to Odysseus.

snapshots.name: Achilles
snapshots.body: The greatest of the Greek warriors at Troy, encountered by Odysseus among the shades of the dead. Odysseus finds him among the fallen heroes of the war they both survived, in Achilles's case only to die there.

snapshots.name: Aeolus
snapshots.body: Keeper of the winds, who hosts Odysseus and gives him a bag containing all the winds that might blow him off course. His gift is nearly wasted through his crew's mistrust before the voyage is over.

snapshots.name: Melanthius
snapshots.body: A goatherd in Odysseus's household who has thrown in his lot with the suitors against his absent master. His disloyalty stands in deliberate contrast to Eumaeus's steadfastness.
